argument_reasoning: The shell command built on line 54 interpolates FIVE opts fields into the same string: sqlclPath, connectString, directory (via path.resolve), appID, destination, and pluginName. Three of them (sqlclPath, destination, pluginName) are wrapped in literal double quotes; two (connectString and appID) are concatenated with only a space on each side. opts.directory is additionally normalized by path.resolve, which collapses path separators and could rewrite the sentinel; opts.destination is first lowercased for the switch, but the ORIGINAL value is interpolated at line 61, so case is preserved. The cleanest injection point is opts.connectString: no quoting, no escaping, no resolve/lowercase pass, so bytes we hand the fuzzer reach execSync verbatim. Jazzer's CommandInjection detector plants the ASCII sentinel "jaz_zer" via libFuzzer compare-trap dictionary, then flags any child_process call whose command string contains that substring -- jaz_zer has no shell metacharacter that would be rewritten anywhere upstream, so it survives through the string concatenation. We use provider.consumeRemainingAsString() for maximum entropy and strip NUL bytes with .replace(/�/g, "") because Node's child_process rejects commands containing NULs with TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE] -- that TypeError is NOT caught by publish()'s try/catch at the right layer (it is actually caught, but it also starves libFuzzer of signal because the exec body is never reached). opts.directory must be a path that actually exists on disk; we create an empty directory under the target package and pass its absolute path. opts.appID is a plain non-empty string ("100") so the "undefined is required" guard at line 26 passes.

lessons: 7B v4 marked this as confirm_gap (reached sink but did not confirm). Likely reasons the local model stops short of a crash-confirmed harness: (1) It picks the WRONG injection channel. opts.sqlclPath, opts.destination and opts.pluginName are all wrapped in literal double quotes in the interpolation (e.g. '"' + opts.sqlclPath + '"'), so the model may reason "this is quoted, so command injection is impossible here" and stop; but it can equally reach the sink via opts.connectString, which is interpolated with just a space on each side and no quoting at all. The lesson is to enumerate EVERY concatenated field and pick the one with the least sanitation, not the first field that happens to be a string. (2) It misses that opts.directory must EXIST on disk (fs.existsSync at line 34). Passing a non-existent path like "/tmp/does-not-exist" or an empty string makes publish() throw before reaching line 54, so the sink is never evaluated and no command string is built. The harness must create an on-disk directory (or point at an always-existing path like "/") and pass its absolute path, otherwise coverage caps at line 35 and the fuzzer looks "stuck" from the outside. (3) It can be confused by the fact that publish() wraps the execSync call in try/catch and swallows errors. The model may believe that any thrown error -- including Jazzer's FuzzerError -- is swallowed and that the detector therefore cannot fire. In fact @jazzer.js/bug-detectors reports the finding via per-iteration state (reportFinding -> ongoing finding) BEFORE throwing, so Jazzer still records the crash even when the throw is caught upstream; the harness only needs to re-throw if a FuzzerError happens to leak up (defense in depth), not to prevent the swallow.
